title: Cisplatin + etoposide with radiotherapy
purpose: Chemotherapy and radiotherapy work together to treat limited-stage small-cell lung cancer. Your team explains the aim and why this combined treatment is suitable for you.

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with cell copying. Fluids and kidney checks help reduce harm to healthy tissue.
agents.watch: Report poor fluid intake, reduced urine, ringing in the ears or numbness.

agents.name: Etoposide
agents.mechanism: Disrupts DNA repair during cell division
agents.explanation: Etoposide blocks an enzyme cells need while copying DNA. The route and prescribed amount differ between infusion and capsules; they are not interchangeable milligram for milligram.
visual: Disrupts DNA repair during cell division
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, severe mouth soreness or vomiting.

phases.label: Four chemotherapy cycles
phases.detail: Reference plan: four 21-day cycles. Day 1: cisplatin and etoposide. Days 2–3: etoposide. Radiotherapy usually starts with cycle 1; its appointments are planned separately. Capsules, split cisplatin, a 28-day interval or a different platinum are used only if explicitly prescribed.

phases.label: Radiotherapy alongside chemotherapy
phases.detail: Usually begins with cycle 1; later start may be appropriate. The radiation team confirms dose, number of visits and timing. A chemotherapy delay does not automatically mean radiation stops.

phases.label: Recovery and response review
phases.detail: After treatment, your team checks recovery, persistent symptoms and response. Scan type/timing and any useful tumour-marker testing are individual decisions; this regimen does not specify a universal scan or marker timetable.

timeline.label: Cisplatin + etoposide
timeline.text: Reference Day 1 IV treatment plus hydration.

timeline.label: Etoposide Days 2–3
timeline.text: IV each day, or prescribed oral alternative. Split cisplatin only if explicitly prescribed.

timeline.label: Symptoms and separate RT plan
timeline.text: Symptoms may occur on any day. This is not a radiation-fraction schedule or a precise low-blood-count curve.

day_groups.title: Day 1: reference combination
day_groups.body: Blood results, symptoms, anti-sickness medicines and hydration are checked before both drugs.
day_groups.action: Tell the nurse about any hearing, nerve or fluid-intake problems.

day_groups.title: Days 2–3: etoposide
day_groups.body: IV treatment each day or prescribed capsules twice daily. The split-cisplatin alternative changes these visits.
day_groups.action: Use your written prescription; do not add IV and oral etoposide together.

day_groups.title: Support and recovery
day_groups.body: No routine chemotherapy in the reference plan. Follow ongoing anti-sickness medicines and separate RT appointments.
day_groups.action: Call early for poor intake, vomiting, swallowing pain or fever.

day_groups.title: Between chemotherapy cycles
day_groups.body: Fatigue, mouth symptoms and infection risk can persist. RT may continue according to its own plan.
day_groups.action: Report symptoms when they occur; do not wait for the next blood test.

support.title: Fluids and sickness prevention
support.text: Cisplatin needs a planned fluid and anti-sickness course. Follow the labelled medicines for each treatment day and the days afterwards. Call if vomiting prevents drinking or taking medicines.

support.title: If capsules are prescribed
support.text: Etoposide capsules on Days 2–3 replace the IV doses on those days. Take the prescribed amount twice daily on an empty stomach. Follow pharmacy handling instructions and contact the team if a dose is missed or vomited; do not take an extra dose without advice.

support.title: Radiotherapy support
support.text: Ask about swallowing, eating, skin care and fatigue during radiation. Painful swallowing or poor intake needs early help; inability to drink needs urgent assessment.

questions.q: Which drugs and routes are prescribed for me?
questions.a: Confirm the exact drug names, routes and interval against your written prescription. The team must explain any change from this reference plan.

questions.q: How do my radiation appointments fit around chemotherapy?
questions.a: Radiation has its own calendar. Ask for the combined plan and whom to contact if a chemotherapy or radiation visit changes.

questions.q: Which blood tests are required before the next dose?
questions.a: Use the checks table as a prompt. Your team confirms which tests are needed, where they are done and who reviews the results before treatment.

questions.q: Who do I call during the day and overnight?
questions.a: Ask the team to replace the example numbers on your card with the correct daytime, overnight and backup contact routes before you leave.

questions.q: When will recovery and response be reviewed?
questions.a: Agree the follow-up appointments and any scans with your team. This regimen does not set a universal scan or tumour-marker timetable.

context_label: Limited-stage small-cell lung cancer · combined chemotherapy and radiation
schedule_summary: Reference plan: four 21-day cycles. Day 1: cisplatin and etoposide. Days 2–3: etoposide. Radiotherapy usually starts with cycle 1; its appointments are planned separately. Capsules, split cisplatin, a 28-day interval or a different platinum are used only if explicitly prescribed.
administration_text: Reference IV plan: etoposide first on Days 1–3, cisplatin after etoposide on Day 1, each infusion about one hour plus checks and fluids. If prescribed, Days 2–3 etoposide may instead be capsules twice daily. Confirm route, platinum, interval and hydration before treatment; never combine alternatives yourself.
monitoring_summary: Blood count, kidney and liver tests before treatment. Hearing tests and a formal kidney-clearance test if clinically indicated; confirm radiation suitability. Blood count, kidney and liver tests before each cycle; ask about hearing changes and numbness before each cycle. After treatment, your team checks recovery, persistent symptoms and response. Scan type/timing and any useful tumour-marker testing are individual decisions; this regimen does not specify a universal scan or marker timetable.
urgent_extra: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, sudden illness, new breathlessness, uncontrolled vomiting, inability to swallow fluids, much less urine or unusual bleeding. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or heavy bleeding needs emergency care. Tell staff immediately about infusion pain, swelling or allergy symptoms.
consent_support: Discuss serious infection/sepsis and possible hospital admission, bleeding, infusion reactions, lung inflammation, painful swallowing/dehydration, fatigue, fertility, hair loss and individual material risks. Cisplatin kidney injury, hearing loss and neuropathy may persist; oral etoposide alternatives need separate handling and dosing explanation. Radiotherapy needs its own informed-consent discussion; chemotherapy consent does not replace it.

chronology_notes.title: Relative schedule, not personal dates
chronology_notes.text: Reference plan: four 21-day cycles. Day 1: cisplatin and etoposide. Days 2–3: etoposide. Radiotherapy usually starts with cycle 1; its appointments are planned separately. Capsules, split cisplatin, a 28-day interval or a different platinum are used only if explicitly prescribed.

chronology_notes.title: Radiation is a separate schedule
chronology_notes.text: Chemotherapy Day 1/Day 2/Day 3 or weekly counts are not radiation fractions. The radiation oncology team supplies the exact RT timetable.

chronology_notes.title: No fixed symptom day
chronology_notes.text: Sickness, fatigue, low counts, swallowing problems or breathing symptoms can occur between visits and after treatment. Do not wait for a calendar window to seek advice.

timeline_note: Reference cycle without patient dates. RT visits and dose are separately prescribed; the symptom band is not a nadir prediction.
safety_note: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, sudden illness, new breathlessness, uncontrolled vomiting, inability to swallow fluids, much less urine or unusual bleeding. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or heavy bleeding needs emergency care. Tell staff immediately about infusion pain, swelling or allergy symptoms.
passport_visit_note: Bring your contact card and medication list. Record each chemotherapy treatment and separately confirm the radiation appointments.

anatomy: Report ringing, reduced hearing, numbness or weakness before the next dose.
Soreness may affect food and fluids. Contact the team early; inability to drink is urgent.
New or worsening breathlessness needs urgent assessment, including after treatment finishes.
Follow the anti-sickness plan. Call if vomiting continues or fluids will not stay down.
Blood tests and fluids protect kidneys. Report much less urine or poor intake.
Fever or sudden illness can be serious. Report bleeding or infusion pain promptly.

monitoring_schedule.title: My tests and treatment checks
monitoring_schedule.note: Required safety tests are distinct from team-agreed imaging and follow-up; no universal tumour-marker interval is specified.

sections.title: Confirm your plan
sections.text: Reference IV plan: etoposide first on Days 1–3, cisplatin after etoposide on Day 1, each infusion about one hour plus checks and fluids. If prescribed, Days 2–3 etoposide may instead be capsules twice daily. Confirm route, platinum, interval and hydration before treatment; never combine alternatives yourself.

sections.title: Keep the contact card
sections.text: The team supplies the daytime and out-of-hours numbers. Keep the card with you and show it when seeking medical care.

sections.title: Two linked treatment teams
sections.text: Confirm which team to contact for radiation or chemotherapy changes. Report swallowing problems early and ask about transport, nutrition and fatigue support.

evidence.title: Why chemotherapy and radiotherapy are combined
evidence.intro: Studies support combining systemic treatment with radiation in the relevant lung-cancer setting.
evidence.interpretation: The evidence comes from specific treatment schedules and patient groups. Your team explains how it applies to your situation; study averages cannot predict an individual outcome.

patient_summary.purpose: Chemotherapy and radiation work together to treat limited-stage small-cell lung cancer. Your team explains your treatment aim and choices.
patient_summary.schedule: Reference IV plan: four 21-day cycles. Day 1: cisplatin + etoposide. Days 2–3: etoposide. Radiation follows its own appointments. Capsules, split cisplatin, carboplatin substitution or 28-day cycles require a different personalised prescription.

phases.title: Chemotherapy
phases.text: Three treatment days per reference cycle, then recovery. Your team confirms each cycle after safety checks.

phases.title: Radiotherapy
phases.text: Usually starts with cycle 1. Radiation oncology sets the dose and visits; chemotherapy delays need separate coordination.

phases.title: After treatment
phases.text: Your team reviews recovery, persistent symptoms and response. Scan or marker timing is individual.

preparation: Confirm your prescription, radiation appointments and blood tests.
Bring your medicine list and daytime / overnight contact numbers.
patient_summary.card_schedule: Day 1: both drugs. Days 2–3: etoposide. Usually every 21 days ×4; RT plan separate.
patient_summary.card_alert: I am receiving chemotherapy with radiotherapy. Fever or sudden illness needs urgent oncology advice.
cycle_expectations: Follow the prescribed anti-sickness course and fluid advice; call early if eating or drinking becomes difficult.
Fever, new breathlessness, uncontrolled vomiting or inability to drink needs urgent advice, including after treatment ends.

treatment_scope_notice: For limited-stage lung cancer: IV cisplatin/etoposide every 21 days. Oral, split-dose, carboplatin or 28-day plans need personalised information.
phases_note: The chemotherapy course is finite; radiotherapy timing and next treatment are confirmed separately.
anatomy_note: This map highlights symptoms to discuss; it does not show how likely an effect is or replace the full consent discussion.
teachback: Explain back your chemotherapy days, how radiation is scheduled separately, the tests before treatment and whom you will call if unwell.
